ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF) Articles L. 561-2-2, L. 561-5 to L. 561-10, L. 561-45 to L. 561-49 and R. 561-1 to R. 561-25; Decree No. 2017-1094 of 8 June 2017 on the Beneficial Owner Register; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); ACPR joint instruction on AML/CFT; TRACFIN implementing regulations under CMF Articles L. 561-1 et seq.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Business Registration Certificate of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., SAMR for China; Companies Registry for Hong Kong; Secretary of State for US entities)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (recent extract) of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution of each foreign corporate shareholder approving the incorporation of the French SAS, approving the articles of association, and appointing the President and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder, notarized by a local notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (procuration) in favor of the designated French attorney and/or the President of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder, signed by its legal representative and notarized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address (utility bill or tax notice dated within 3 months) of all natural-person beneficial owners and the President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary public or issuing authority in the UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate blocking the share capital funds (attestation de blocage de fonds) issued upon opening the provisional capital account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed French or EU credit institution (passporting into France)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: None - original bank-signed certificate accepted without apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory auditor's report on contributions in kind (rapport du commissaire aux apports), if non-cash contributions exceed EUR 7,500 in value and no unanimous shareholder waiver applies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Statutory auditor registered with the Compagnie Nationale des Commissaires aux Comptes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under CMF Articles L. 561-5 and L. 561-6; systematic screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists under Council Decision 2001/931/CFSP and Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001, (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (iii) OFAC SDN list for advisory standards on USD clearing, and (iv) TRACFIN typological PEP risk indicators; identification and verification of Politically Exposed Persons per CMF Article L. 561-10 with enhanced due diligence and senior management approval; beneficial owner declaration (RBE) must be filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within 30 days of incorporation under CMF Article R. 561-1 and updated within 30 days of any material change; intentional non-disclosure is punishable by up to 2 years imprisonment and EUR 30,000 fine for natural persons and up to EUR 150,000 for legal entities under CMF Article L. 561-49.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by the INPI; official company registry (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) extracts and name availability checks are performed via infogreffe.fr; trademark and name pre-screening via INPI Data (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (dénomination sociale) must be stated in the articles of association, must be lawful, available, and not misleading (Code de commerce Articles L. 210-1 and R. 123-53); all corporate documents and statutory filings must be in French under Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Toubon Law, Article 2); the name must be written in Latin script; a foreign word, invented word, or transliteration may be accepted provided it is distinctive, phonetically usable in French, and not contrary to public order; where a foreign-language name is used, the French transliteration governs legal documents and RCS registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Établissement de crédit (reserved for credit institutions licensed by ACPR)
Assurance / Insurance (reserved for insurers licensed by ACPR)
Mutuelle / Caisse d'assurance mutuelle (reserved for mutual insurers)
Société de gestion / Gestion de portefeuille (reserved for AMF-licensed asset managers)
Fonds de pension / Fonds de retraite (reserved, requires supervisory authorization)
Ministère / République / Président / Préfecture (sovereign authority terms contrary to public order)
EDF / RTE / Enedis / Engie (state-controlled energy operator denominations protected against misappropriation)
Chambre de commerce / Chambre des métiers (reserved for public-law chambers)
Trust (reserved for licensed trust-type entities under CMF Article L. 547-1)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory binding name-reservation system; the name becomes protected only upon effective RCS registration, and the statutory publication in a Journal d'annonces légales opens a 30-day opposition window for third-party prior-right holders under Article L. 711-4 of the Intellectual Property Code and RCS distinctiveness case law. Upon rejection by the Greffe, the applicant may: (1) submit a modified name through the Guichet Unique within 30 days of the refusal; (2) file a gracieux recourse with the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce requesting a reasoned waiver; (3) bring a judicial action before the Tribunal judiciaire under Code de commerce Article L. 123-5 to challenge the registry's refusal as ultra vires; (4) in trademark conflict cases, initiate an opposition proceeding before the INPI within 2 months of publication of a conflicting trademark application, or an action for nullity before the Tribunal judiciaire if a prior mark is invoked; the Greffe must process compliant remote filings within 5 working days under the Guichet Unique procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for a non-licensing B2B hardware company at incorporation: the registered office (siège social) may be domiciled at the residence of the legal representative for a maximum of 5 years (Code de commerce Article L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-13) or with a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) approved by the Prefecture. However, a purely virtual office without operational decision-making, local accounting presence, or storage/assembly facilities may trigger re-characterization by the DGFiP for VAT registration purposes (Bofip BOI-CF-RES-40-10-20) and increase transfer-pricing audit exposure; a physical lease or serviced office is recommended within 12 months after the first invoiced sale in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified at 5% within the first 24 months for a low-risk B2B hardware manufacturer with no unusual VAT refund claims and no R&D tax credit (CIR) application; the DGFiP may conduct unannounced premises visits (visites domiciliaires) only under judicial warrant per Livre des procédures fiscales Article L. 16B when there are serious indicators of hidden activity or tax fraud; ordinary accounting verification audits (vérification de comptabilité) are initiated by written notice, with an estimated SME audit rate of approximately 0.8% annually; strict adherence to RBE filing and statutory publication deadlines materially reduces audit-trigger probability.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark at EUR 350-450/hour; flat fee for SAS incorporation between EUR 2,000 and EUR 4,000 excluding disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee of EUR 150-250 per search report covering 2 classes and official search databases

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) of the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved legal gazette (e.g., Petites Affiches, VILA, or departmental JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by ministerial order, from EUR 48 to EUR 120 per insertion depending on department and text length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fee (droit d'enregistrement du Greffe) including one-stop-shop handling via Guichet Unique

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public and competent apostille authority (e.g., China Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Hong Kong High Court Authentication Section)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official foreign scale tariffs: USD 45-80 per notarized packet plus USD 10-30 per apostille; assumed batch of 3-4 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation (traduction assermentée) of all apostilled corporate documents and UBO passport copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (expert près une cour d'appel) listed at the relevant Court of Appeal

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II — Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-27 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) in conjunction with Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10; implementing regulations in Articles R. 227-1 to R. 227-12; creation and filing regime reformed by Decree No. 2021-1736 of 22 December 2021 (Guichet Unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) of the registered-office district, operating through the national Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises developed by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de Création d'Entreprise (electronic M0-type declaration) accompanied by the signed Articles of Association (Statuts, private-pact or notarial deed), the funds-deposit attestation, the legal-notice certificate, and the beneficial-owner declaration; final proof of registration is the Extrait K-Bis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to the SAS; the Articles set the capital freely. At least 50% of cash subscriptions must be paid up at subscription and the remaining 50% within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a French credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; funds are released strictly upon production of the Extrait K-Bis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY SAS] — adopted this [date] by the founding shareholder(s) and President pursuant to Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-27 of the French Commercial Code. RESOLVED: (1) the share capital of EUR [amount] is fully subscribed and the cash contributions have been paid up and deposited in a blocked account in accordance with statutory escrow rules, to be released only upon RCS registration; (2) the registered office is established at [address], within the jurisdiction of the Commercial Court Registry of [city], with proof of occupancy to be filed; (3) [name] is appointed President, authorized to represent the Company, open bank accounts, and complete all registration and regulatory filings. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and certification of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire of the registered-office department (notarial form) or the founding shareholders under private-pact deed (acte sous seing privé); documents are later filed through the INPI Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, covering legal form (SAS), corporate name, purpose (manufacture, installation, and aftermarket maintenance of high-power DC ultra-fast electric vehicle chargers), 99-year duration, registered office, share capital, share classes, president, governance, and allocation of shares. Have each founder verify identity and legal capacity, and sign the deed; where notarial form is elected, schedule attendance or legal representation at the notary act. If any in-kind contribution is present, appoint and attach the statutory contribution auditor's report (commissaire aux apports).
required_dossiers: Draft and final Statuts (acte sous seing privé or notarial deed)
Identity documents (valid passports or national ID) of all founders
Power of attorney for represented founders
Proof of address for each founder
Certified translation of any foreign-language document
Contribution auditor's report (rapport du commissaire aux apports) where non-cash contributions exist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Guichet Unique raises a formal defect (e.g., missing clause on share transfer restrictions or president's powers), an amending deed (acte rectificatif) is executed by the shareholders and annexed to the e-dossier before the filing is perfected; no fresh incorporation is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and deposit of share capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (banque dépositaire), Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary authorized to hold escrow funds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional blocked account in the name of the company in formation and remit the cash contributions. Require the depositary to issue an attestation de dépôt des fonds and a subscription schedule (état récapitulatif des souscriptions). Verify that at least 50% of the subscribed cash capital is released; the depositary maintains the block until the K-Bis is presented, at which time the funds are transferred to the company's free operating account.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts or certified draft
Bank account-opening forms and KYC documents
Shareholder subscription schedule
Proof of source of funds for each subscribing shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation is refused or delayed because of KYC incompleteness, supply the requested compliance documentation; if the deposit instruction fails, re-issue the wire and obtain a corrected certificate. Where the company is not registered within the statutory period, the depositary returns the funds to subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) duly authorized by the prefecture of the department in which the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit the avis de constitution showing the exact legal form (SAS), corporate name, capital amount, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, share classes and number, president's identity, and the competent commercial court. Upon publication, obtain the attestation de parution, which is mandatory for the subsequent RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Text of the incorporation notice
Final Statuts (for verification by the JAL)
Statement of share capital and classes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains an error or is rejected by the JAL, publish a corrective notice (avis rectificatif) with exact rectified particulars and file the new attestation with the Guichet Unique; the greffe accepts the rectificatif where it modifies only non-material data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the creation dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the INPI and transmitted for public-order control to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office district.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the declaration on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, selecting the SAS as legal form and ISIC 2930 / manufacture of EV chargers as activity; upload the final Statuts, deposit attestation, JAL certificate, occupancy proof, identity documents, and the beneficial-owner declaration (DBE); pay the greffe filing fee online; retain the electronic acknowledgement of receipt. The greffe performs legal, capacity, and non-confusion checks and orders inscription in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic creation declaration (M0-equivalent)
Final signed Statuts (PDF)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Registered-office occupancy proof (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Identity documents of legal representatives
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE) and supporting capacity evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique returns the dossier as incomplete or irregular, the declarant receives an online query and must cure the deficiency within the stated deadline; if the greffe refuses inscription on substantive grounds, the founders may request a review by the presiding judge of the commercial court (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) or re-file after rectification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — income tax and VAT; operational portals impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel, TéléTVA) and Chorus Pro (choruspro.gouv.fr) for e-invoicing; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — customs/import VAT/export, portal douane.gouv.fr (DELTA); VIES validation: ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic SAS: one single filing with the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) triggers RCS registration and INSEE issue of SIREN/SIRET and automatic notification to DGFiP; no separate TIN filing. DGFiP assigns the French intra-Community VAT number using the format FR + 11 digits (last nine = SIREN). A non-established foreign entity carrying out French taxable supplies must file Form 3514-SD (Cerfa no. 15823) with the DGFiP non-resident office (SIE Non-Résidents), appointing a fiscal representative where Article 289 A CGI requires it; proof: Kbis extract, INSEE 'Avis de situation', DGFiP VAT identification notice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box/pass-through election exists for an SAS; an SAS is irrebuttably opaque and subject to corporation tax (IS). Available elections: (1) French tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223A for a French parent holding at least 95% of a French subsidiary; (2) parent-subsidiary participation exemption (régime mère-fille, CGI Arts. 145/216) for qualifying shareholdings of at least 5%; (3) territoriality option under CGI Art. 209-I to exclude profits of eligible foreign permanent establishments; (4) optional single VAT taxpayer grouping (assujetti unique TVA, CGI Art. 256-C-III); (5) CFC rules (Art. 209-B CGI) and hybrid-mismatch provisions (Art. 209-II-bis CGI) are mandatory rather than elective.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, within the Eurosystem; foreign-exchange policy is principally governed by the European Union, the European Central Bank, French monetary and financial legislation, and the French Treasury. Prudential and conduct supervision of banks and payment institutions is principally performed by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, customs, foreign-investment-control, and reporting requirements. A French SAS may generally receive foreign capital, pay foreign suppliers, repatriate dividends, repay documented shareholder loans, and transfer operating profits offshore without a general exchange-control approval. Dividend distributions require distributable profits, approved financial statements, corporate approvals, and applicable withholding-tax analysis. Interest, royalties, service fees, and intra-group payments must be commercially justified, arm's-length where applicable, properly documented, and reviewed for withholding tax, beneficial ownership, transfer pricing, deductibility, and anti-abuse rules. Payments involving sanctioned persons, jurisdictions, dual-use goods, or controlled technology may require blocking, licensing, or enhanced review. Foreign direct investment authorization may apply to activities falling within French protected sectors; ordinary manufacture of EV charging equipment is generally outside the protected sectors unless the business also involves regulated energy infrastructure, critical technologies, national-security-sensitive systems, or other controlled activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may normally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's treasury discretion. The company must retain commercial, customs, invoicing, transport, and payment records and comply with applicable Intrastat, customs, statistical, tax, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering reporting obligations. Individual banks may impose contractual documentation, transaction-monitoring, or account-crediting requirements. Cash receipts and certain cross-border payments may trigger French monetary-financial reporting obligations, and bank-specific reporting may apply to transactions involving non-EU jurisdictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in EUR and permitted foreign currencies; capital subscription funds may be held in a temporary blocked capital account pending incorporation or capital increase and then transferred to the operational account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank, acting through the relevant Crédit Agricole group French banking entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in EUR and permitted foreign currencies; temporary capital deposit account available subject to entity-formation or capital-increase documentation and bank acceptance.
Operational current account in EUR and permitted foreign currencies; temporary blocked account for subscribed share capital may be available before registration or capital increase.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group French banking entity, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne network entity selected for the company's location
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account in EUR and permitted foreign currencies; capital deposit or escrow-like blocked account subject to local entity procedures and proof of incorporation or capital increase.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operating payments and treasury administration, but not a complete substitute for a French commercial-bank relationship. A licensed European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarding, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange services, and sometimes international wire access through regulated correspondent arrangements. It generally cannot provide bank deposits, conventional lending, statutory capital-deposit certificates, or unrestricted cash-management functionality unless separately licensed for those services. Offshore digital EMIs outside the EEA cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services to French customers merely through an offshore application; they require an applicable French or EEA authorization, passporting basis, or authorized local arrangement. EMI onboarding may be restricted for high-value capital injections, complex ownership chains, non-EEA counterparties, cash-intensive activity, sanctioned-country exposure, or transactions requiring documentary trade-finance review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding and electronic identification may be available, especially for standard-risk French SAS entities, but the bank determines the procedure. Banks may require a live video interview, certified identification, qualified electronic signatures, original or apostilled corporate documents, a French registered-office verification, and an in-person meeting for non-resident shareholders, complex ownership, higher-risk jurisdictions, unusual business models, capital deposits, trade finance, or unresolved beneficial-owner issues. At least one authorized representative should be prepared to complete enhanced verification in French or English. Remote onboarding is not guaranteed and may be unavailable until the SAS has been registered and has obtained its SIREN/SIRET and registry extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to identify the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current French registry extract; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart tracing every entity to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and residential-address evidence for beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories; certified corporate documents for each corporate shareholder; beneficial-owner declaration filed with the competent French registry; board authorization and powers of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent, shareholder, director, or group treasury center with limited French operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent-group ownership and governance documents; certificates of incorporation and tax residence; audited financial statements or management accounts; group organization chart; explanation of the French SAS business purpose; expected transaction profile; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; intercompany funding agreement; capital contribution resolution; projected cash-flow statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound shareholder funding or loan proceeds inconsistent with stated share capital and forecast turnover.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; lender or parent bank statements; evidence of originating account ownership; audited accounts; funding-flow diagram; commercial rationale; transfer-pricing analysis where relevant; confirmation of the exact payment purpose; sanctions and beneficial-owner screening records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, politically exposed persons, or opaque intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC pack; beneficial-owner identification; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user statement; contracts, purchase orders, invoices, shipping records, customs documents, and certificates of origin; independent due-diligence report; documented approval by compliance and treasury; applicable sanctions or export-control license.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EV charging equipment activity that appears connected to critical infrastructure, government procurement, dual-use technology, cybersecurity, or regulated energy operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product catalogue and technical specifications; statement that the company manufactures hardware rather than operates regulated electricity networks unless otherwise applicable; customer and end-use profile; export-control classification; cybersecurity and product-compliance certifications; public-procurement documentation; analysis of French foreign-investment-control and sector-license applicability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume international trade without established suppliers, customers, logistics flows, or customs history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier and customer master file; signed distribution, manufacturing, and supply agreements; purchase orders; sales pipeline; Incoterms; transport and insurance arrangements; customs-broker appointment; sample commercial invoices; expected monthly payment volumes, currencies, countries, and counterparties; treasury policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash settlement, virtual assets, unexplained third-party payments, or payment instructions inconsistent with contractual counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal and cash settlement; approved payment matrix; segregation-of-duties policy; bank-account verification controls; third-party-payment approval procedure; accounting records; reconciliation reports; explanation and remediation evidence for any historical exception.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, CRS, FATCA, VAT, or economic-substance inconsistencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax identification details; CRS and FATCA self-certifications; VAT registration or application evidence; French registered-office and lease evidence; payroll or operational plan; tax-residence certificates for relevant entities; intercompany agreements; explanation of permanent-establishment and management-location analysis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscriptions for SAS share capital through a French bank or another institution authorized to issue the required capital-deposit certificate. Use a blocked capital account before incorporation or a capital increase, identify the subscriber and the French SAS precisely, and state the legal purpose as share-capital subscription or capital increase. After registration or completion of the capital increase, provide the Kbis or equivalent registry evidence, updated articles or capital records, shareholder and board resolutions, and the capital-deposit certificate so funds can be released to the operational account. Route shareholder loans through a documented intercompany-loan or financing agreement, with arm's-length terms, lender and borrower account ownership evidence, transfer-pricing support, and any required French loan, tax, or statistical filings. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro transfers within the SEPA area and SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 payment messaging for non-SEPA wires. Include complete originator, beneficiary, IBAN or account number, BIC where applicable, purpose narrative, invoice or agreement reference, and UBO-consistent payer details. Do not split payments to avoid screening or reporting. Reconcile each receipt to the general ledger and retain the payment trail, contracts, bank statements, and accounting evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 cross-border payment instructions for non-SEPA currencies and jurisdictions. For documentary trade finance, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit transmitted through authenticated bank channels, typically SWIFT MT700, with amendments through the issuing and advising banks; use confirmed letters of credit where country or bank risk warrants confirmation. Match payment instructions to purchase orders, contracts, invoices, Incoterms, customs declarations, transport documents, insurance documents, certificates of origin, and sanctions or export-control screening. For open-account trade, use controlled supplier onboarding, dual approval, verified beneficiary-account changes, payment limits, and three-way matching. The French SAS should maintain EUR as the primary operating currency, establish approved foreign-currency accounts where commercially necessary, and document any conversion spread, bank fee, withholding-tax treatment, VAT treatment, and hedge designation. No French foreign-exchange approval is generally required for ordinary commercial imports or exports, but banks may request evidence for AML, sanctions, customs, tax, and transaction-monitoring purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts with an authorized EU bank or investment firm, supported by a documented underlying exposure, approved dealing limits, confirmation procedures, valuation, collateral terms where applicable, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are non-convertible or subject to local settlement restrictions, provided the counterparty is appropriately regulated, the transaction is lawful in the relevant jurisdiction, sanctions and local-market rules are satisfied, and the hedge is linked to a genuine exposure rather than speculative trading.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or cash-flow exposures, subject to counterparty eligibility, ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral and margin requirements, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation obligations where applicable, and internal approval.

Currency options, collars, and participating forwards where permitted by the authorized counterparty and suitable for the company's risk profile, with documented suitability, premium, valuation, limit, and accounting controls.

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency revenues and costs, centralized netting, foreign-currency cash pooling where legally and contractually available, and intercompany settlement netting supported by transfer-pricing and treasury documentation.

Hedging governance should prohibit unsupported speculation, define approved currencies and counterparties, require exposure forecasts and hedge ratios, apply segregation of dealing, confirmation, settlement, and valuation functions, and preserve confirmations, valuations, collateral records, EMIR or other regulatory reports, and board-approved treasury-policy evidence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (comptes annuels) with shareholders' approval and deposit with the Trade and Companies Register (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year close for shareholder approval; deposit within 1 month of approval (maximum 7 months after the close for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 4,500 for companies with more than 250 employees); interest and court-ordered penalties; persistent default may trigger non-availability of legal certificate and ultimately forced strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual financial statement annex (liasse fiscale n°2065, annex n°2065/CIT) including results and balance sheet schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: 2nd working day after 1 May of the following year (electronic filing is mandatory); for non-calendar fiscal years: no later than the 2nd working day of the fifth month following the close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed corporate tax, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; additional 10% surcharge after a formal 30-day notice; non-filing after demand can lead to enforcement resulting in administrative penalty and, in extreme cases, criminal sanction for tax evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of corporate officers, share capital, registered office and beneficial owners (RCS annual regulatory declaration upon any change, and minimum triennial UBO verification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial UBO declaration within 15 days of registration; mandatory update within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or corporate particulars; annual internal verification of registered data is required for the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for failure to update UBO information up to EUR 5,000 for individuals and EUR 30,000 for companies; legal representative may face confiscation of powers; administrative warning precedes strike-off proceedings for continued non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a certified public auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SAS if it exceeds two of the following three thresholds at the close of the fiscal year for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8 million, and an average workforce exceeding 50 employees; certain groups and listed entities are audited irrespective of thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan Comptable Général, PCG). Consolidated accounts may be prepared under IFRS. All registers and accounts are maintained in EUR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In a French SAS, beneficial owners must be identified and documented at inception and the corresponding declaration filed with the RCS. Any change in beneficial ownership must be declared to the RCS within 30 days. Although no annual statutory re-filing of the UBO declaration is generally required if no change occurs, the legal representative must verify the register each year at the shareholders' ordinary meeting, confirm there has been no change or obtain corrected UBO data, and retain the internal verification in the corporate minute book. Share transfers must be recorded in the share-transfer register and the register of members to maintain accurate voting and dividend allocation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Securities (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors and Supervisory Board Meetings (Registre des décisions et délibérations)
Minutes of General Meetings (Registre des assemblées générales)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 6,000 per year for a small or mid-sized SAS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, provided that turnover does not exceed EUR 10 million, capital is fully paid up, and at least 75% of the share capital is held by qualifying individuals or qualifying companies. The standard 25% rate applies above that threshold. Additional credits and deductions may apply depending on qualifying research, innovation, energy-transition, apprenticeship, and investment expenditure. France generally does not provide a general corporate tax holiday for ordinary EV-charger manufacturing.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited under French law, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Tax losses may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits and an election.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_base_and_surcharges: Taxable profit is determined from statutory accounts, subject to French tax adjustments. Large companies may be subject to the social contribution on corporate income tax, generally 3.3% of corporate income tax after the statutory allowance, where the relevant corporate income tax liability exceeds EUR 763,000. Temporary exceptional surcharges may apply only if enacted for the relevant tax year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2065-SD, Déclaration de résultats - Impôt sur les sociétés, with the applicable corporate tax package, including Forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, and balance-sheet, income-statement, and fixed-asset schedules. Electronic filing is generally mandatory through the impots.gouv.fr professional account using EDI-TDFC or an authorized accounting software provider. Payment is made electronically through the professional tax account.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; four provisional corporate income tax installments are generally due annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the statutory filing deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May of the following year. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, it is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, tax office, financial-year opening and closing dates, and filing period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS legal name and SIREN exactly as registered. Report the French entity, not the foreign shareholder or parent. Identify any French permanent establishment separately where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax regime, tax-consolidation status, and applicable special regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the ordinary corporate income tax regime unless a valid tax-consolidation, merger, group, or special-regime election exists. Non-resident ownership does not by itself change the French SAS filing regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax adjustments, depreciation differences, provisions, and other additions or deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-parent accounting entries unless booked by the French SAS. Reconcile related-party charges, withholding taxes, permanent-establishment allocations, and non-deductible expenses under French rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses generated in prior periods, losses utilized in the current period, losses carried forward, and any elected loss carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a period-by-period loss schedule. Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% utilization cap and do not treat accounting losses as automatically equivalent to tax losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, tax reductions, foreign tax credits where available, and other tax attributes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by French eligibility conditions and contemporaneous documentation. Foreign taxes are not automatically creditable and may instead be governed by an applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, capital losses, and the applicable tax treatment for disposals of assets and securities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify disposals by asset type and holding period. Review treaty allocation where French real estate, a French permanent establishment, or real-estate-rich shares are involved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation and tracking of taxable and deferred capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document any merger, contribution, rollover, or deferral regime and retain the required legal and valuation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special categories of gains, including qualifying participation and other regulated categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply participation-exemption rules only after verifying ownership, holding-period, classification, and recapture requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Receivables, payables, cash, debt, provisions, inventory, and other balance-sheet positions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile intercompany balances to counterparties and disclose foreign-currency positions using the applicable French accounting and tax treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital movements, ownership information, and related statutory data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record foreign shareholders accurately and maintain beneficial-owner and ownership-chain evidence. Ownership data must agree with corporate registers and UBO filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of certain non-deductible or exceptional expenses, including specified executive compensation, attendance fees, and other regulated expenses where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review payments to directors, officers, and related foreign persons for deductibility, disclosure, and transfer-pricing implications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration where the statutory thresholds and conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose material controlled transactions and ensure consistency with the Local File, Master File, intercompany agreements, invoices, and accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payment and balance settlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay electronically from the French professional tax account. Monitor installment credits, tax credits, withholding offsets, and any group-tax allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, which may increase to 40% after formal notice and to 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules, in addition to applicable surcharges. Inaccurate returns may trigger penalties of 40% for deliberate breach and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law. Failure to file required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by the missing documentation, with additional tax adjustments and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax installment payments through the impots.gouv.fr professional account; no separate quarterly corporate income tax return is generally filed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment cycle; no quarterly income tax computation return in the ordinary regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. A company may be exempt from an installment where the preceding-year corporate income tax liability is below the applicable statutory threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, tax account, payment period, tax type, and amount paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS tax account and ensure the payer bank account is authorized for electronic tax payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount calculated by reference to prior-year corporate income tax or the statutory alternative basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile each installment with the prior-year assessment, current-year forecast, tax credits, and any group-tax payment arrangement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate 0.20% monthly interest and a 5% late-payment surcharge where applicable, in addition to enforcement measures. Persistent non-payment may lead to formal notice, forced collection, bank-account seizure, and director-management consequences in cases of serious misconduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic French withholding tax rate on dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident legal entity is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or EEA parent company may be exempt under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring the relevant ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions. Dividends paid to a French corporate shareholder are generally not subject to withholding tax, although participation-exemption and add-back rules apply at recipient level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Confirm the recipient's beneficial ownership, treaty residence, legal status, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose conditions, and minimum ownership requirements. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's tax authority before payment where possible. Provide the French payer with the treaty-relief form or supporting residence documentation required for the relevant treaty and distribution type. Apply the reduced rate only where the payer has adequate evidence; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and permit the recipient to seek a refund from the French tax administration. Retain board resolutions, dividend vouchers, ownership evidence, residence certificates, beneficial-owner analysis, and payment records.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to domestic withholding tax, subject to anti-abuse, debt-characterization, and special-regime rules; an applicable treaty may allocate taxing rights or permit a source-country rate. Royalties and similar payments for the use of intellectual property are generally subject to a domestic withholding tax of 25%, subject to treaty reductions and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where its conditions are satisfied. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and from 0% to 10% or 15% for royalties, but the exact rate depends on the recipient's jurisdiction, beneficial ownership, income classification, and treaty text. Service fees, software payments, equipment rentals, and technical assistance must be classified separately because different French withholding and permanent-establishment rules may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File documentation is generally mandatory where the French entity's annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 400 million, or where it is controlled by, controls, or belongs to a group containing an entity meeting the EUR 400 million threshold. Documentation may also be required under a formal tax audit request. The annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies to entities meeting the relevant EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold or belonging to a qualifying group, subject to the statutory conditions. Separate country-by-country reporting generally applies to the reporting entity of a multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic-substance regime equivalent to a comprehensive ESR applicable to all companies. Substance is assessed through transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-abuse rule, the principal-purpose test in treaties and EU law, controlled foreign company rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, permanent-establishment principles, interest limitation rules, and anti-hybrid rules. A French SAS should maintain adequate French decision-making, personnel, premises, operational assets, risk control, accounting records, banking activity, and commercial evidence proportionate to its EV-charger manufacturing and distribution functions. Conduit entities, circular financing, artificial royalty structures, and arrangements lacking commercial rationale are high-risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.ev_charger_specific_tp_controls: Document ownership and use of patents, firmware, software, trademarks, engineering know-how, warranty risk, product-liability risk, inventory risk, procurement functions, installation support, after-sales service, and market-development activities. Intercompany imports must be reconciled to customs values and transfer prices. Customs valuation, VAT, corporate income tax, and transfer-pricing positions must be mutually consistent or supported by documented differences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of taxable sales, fabricated expenses, concealed cash receipts, false invoices, double accounting, or intentional understatement of taxable profit or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax reassessment, late-payment interest, 40% penalty for deliberate breach, and up to 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law. Tax fraud may be criminally punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine, increasing in aggravated cases to up to seven years and EUR 3 million, subject to the applicable Criminal Code provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability for intentional or grossly negligent misconduct, management-ban orders, and tax-liability transfer under French tax procedure where they made collection impossible through fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated tax-law breaches. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered by a court in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent transfer pricing and profit diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length import pricing, unsupported management fees, excessive royalties, interest stripping, artificial commission arrangements, or allocation of French functions and risks to a foreign affiliate without operational evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under the arm's-length principle, 25% corporate income tax, interest, applicable tax penalties, and documentation penalties. Missing or materially incomplete documentation may trigger the statutory penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of covered transactions, without limiting the reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they knowingly approve sham arrangements, falsified documentation, or deliberate profit concealment. Civil claims may include restitution of losses and damages; criminal exposure depends on proof of fraud, forgery, laundering, or participation in another offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a French SAS as a registered-office conduit with no personnel, premises, decision-making, inventory control, or genuine commercial activity, combined with immediate onward payments to a foreign principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under anti-abuse principles, denial of treaty or EU withholding relief, denial of deductions, withholding-tax assessments, corporate tax reassessment, and applicable penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for breach of management duties and criminal liability if the structure is used for tax fraud, money laundering, forgery, or concealment. A corporate veil is not automatically pierced merely because the company is thinly staffed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of dividends, royalties, interest, service fees, or similar amounts to non-residents without determining French-source status, applying the correct domestic rate, or retaining valid treaty-residence and beneficial-owner evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, late-payment interest, applicable penalties, denial of treaty relief, and potential penalties for inaccurate or missing declarations. The payer may remain liable even where the non-resident recipient received the gross amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal exposure where non-remittance is deliberate, records are falsified, or payments are made to conceal assets or distributions. Ordinary administrative withholding errors normally remain corporate liabilities unless aggravated misconduct is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassification of EV chargers, false customs value, diversion of imported goods, fictitious intra-EU supplies, unsupported VAT exemptions, missing import VAT, or incorrect place-of-supply treatment for installation and maintenance services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT and customs reassessment, import duties, interest, administrative penalties, seizure, and potentially criminal prosecution for organized or deliberate fraud. Customs penalties depend on the offense, goods, value, and applicable Union Customs Code and French customs provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal and civil exposure for intentional customs or VAT fraud, including restitution, fines, management bans, and imprisonment in serious cases. Personal liability is fact-dependent and is not automatic for a routine classification error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, concealing beneficial ownership, processing suspicious wire transfers, using shell suppliers, falsifying trade documents, or failing to identify and report suspicious activity where the business is subject to AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is generally punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated cases subject to higher penalties, including up to ten years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine. Regulated entities may also face supervisory sanctions, including significant monetary penalties, business restrictions, and license consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may be prosecuted for participation, complicity, concealment, or negligent control failures where legally relevant. Courts may order confiscation, asset freezing, management bans, and restrictions on movement; travel bans are discretionary and case-specific.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting fraud and false corporate records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, recognizing fictitious inventory, capitalizing ordinary expenses without basis, concealing related-party balances, or approving accounts that do not provide a true and fair representation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, civil damages, regulatory consequences, and criminal penalties under company and criminal law for falsification, presentation, or publication of inaccurate accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Presidents, directors, de facto managers, and persons approving false accounts may face personal civil liability, criminal fines, imprisonment, management bans, and contribution claims from creditors or insolvency practitioners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal dividend distribution and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without approved accounts, distributing more than distributable reserves, paying dividends while concealing losses, or continuing payments to shareholders while insolvency is foreseeable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful dividends, damages, corporate-law penalties, and possible insolvency proceedings. Directors may be ordered to contribute to insufficient assets where management faults caused or aggravated the deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS president and de facto managers may incur restitution, damages, asset-contribution orders, management bans, and criminal liability for unlawful distributions or bankruptcy-related offenses. A dividend must be supported by properly approved accounts and distributable reserves.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Export controls, sanctions, and dual-use goods
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exporting chargers, power electronics, software, encryption, technical data, or components to restricted jurisdictions or sanctioned parties without screening, authorization, or end-use controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative measures, transaction blocking, asset freezes, customs seizure, significant fines, and criminal penalties under applicable French, European Union, and United Nations sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, management bans, and confiscation where they knowingly authorize prohibited transactions or deliberately ignore sanctions controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payments or benefits to public officials, procurement intermediaries, fleet customers, distributors, or agents to obtain charging-infrastructure contracts, permits, customs treatment, or preferential purchasing decisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal bribery penalties may include imprisonment and substantial fines, confiscation, exclusion from public procurement, and corporate compliance measures. Corporate liability may be imposed independently of individual liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, civil restitution, management bans, and travel restrictions ordered by a court. The Sapin II framework also requires qualifying companies to maintain anti-corruption prevention controls.
